{"concepts_used":["GC-0109","GC-0088","GC-0084","GC-0116","GC-0091","GC-0081"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part34/2#1","quote":"the trade mark must, at the time the application for a defensive registration is filed, already be registered in the name of the applicant;"},{"ref":"TMA1995/s185(1)","quote":"the trade mark may, on the application of the registered owner, be registered as a defensive trade mark in respect of any or all of those other goods or services."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s185(1)","quote":"If, because of the extent to which a registered trade mark has been used in relation to all or any of the goods or services in respect of which it is registered, it is likely that its use in relation to other goods or services will be taken to indicate that there is a connection between those other goods or services and the registered owner of the trade mark"}],"answer":"Check the existing registration and its ownership, but the supplied passages do not establish a separate requirement to check the company’s legal status.

• Manual practice: the basic trade mark must already be registered in the applicant’s name when the defensive application is filed. The check is therefore not merely whether an old registration exists, but whether it is registered in that applicant’s name at that time. [TMM/Part34/2#1]
• Act: section 185(1) provides for defensive registration on the application of the registered owner. It also requires the extent of use of the registered mark to make the relevant connection with that owner likely; ownership alone is not the full test. [TMA1995/s185(1)]

Neither of those supplied passages addresses a separate corporate-status enquiry, such as checking incorporation or deregistration. I cannot confirm from the supplied material whether that additional check is required."}
